items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw and Tommy Dorsey... they was the one to have control of the music... all those big bands that it was so beautiful, so pleasant to dance.

ctx.x: In those days, like in the United States thirty, forty, fifty years ago, the black musician was what - the power in the entertainment field; comedian, dancers, so forth, so on; so the way out to has some - bring some bread and butter to the house is to be a tap dancer like Bill Robinson and ah - Bill Bailey, and the other guy, the other guy, the Nicholas Brothers, the other guy and the other guy, so, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Fletcher Henderson, you name it. They was the one to have control of the music until…
I see. Okay, so then one of the reasons why Afro-Cubans families went for music was probably because it was a way to earn a livelihood and recognition.
